0.headline: Gaja Capital raises Rs 165 crore via anchor book ahead of Rs 550-crore IPO
0.heading: Gaja Capital raises Rs 165 crore via anchor book ahead of Rs 550-crore IPO
0.intro: Gaja Capital IPO | The initial public offering included fresh issuance of equity shares worth Rs 450 crore. The offer also comprises an offer-for-sale amounting to Rs 100 crore by promoters and other selling shareholders.
0.body:
Gaja Alternative Asset Management, the alternative asset management company commercially known as Gaja Capital, has raised Rs 165 crore via anchor book on August 18. This fund raising came in a day before the IPO opening for public subscription on August 19.

The company has approached capital markets with the objective to mobilise up to Rs 550 crore via initial public offering (IPO) which included fresh issuance of equity shares worth Rs 450 crore. The offer also comprises an offer-for-sale amounting to Rs 100 crore by promoters and other selling shareholders.

The price band for the offer, which closes on August 21, has been fixed at Rs 152-160 per share.

Total 15 institutional investors participated in the anchor book on Tuesday including Societe Generale, Ashish Kochalia-backed Bengal Finance and Investments, Ashwin Kumar Kothari group's Winro Commercial (India), and Mukul Agrawal-mentored Sanshi Fund-I.

The allocation of 1.03 crore equity shares has been finalised by Gaja Capital, at the upper end of price band.

Out of the total allocation, it has allocated 67.18 lakh equity shares to seven domestic mutual funds including Nippon Life India, Invesco, JM Financial MF, Groww MF, Helios Mutual Fund, Trust MF, and Samco, which have applied through a 13 schemes.

Insurance companies also showed interest in Gaja Capital as HDFC Life, SBI Life, and Bajaj Life have also decided to pick up 17.18 lakh equity shares worth Rs 27.49 crore.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Gopal Jain, Ranjit Jayant Shah, and Imran Jafar-promoted Gaja Alternative Asset Management will utilise Rs 372 crore of net fresh issue proceeds for investing towards sponsor commitments to certain existing and new funds and for repayment of the bridge loan amount. And the remaining funds will be set aside for general corporate purposes.

The company that acts as an investment manager to India focused funds - category II and category I alternative investment funds (AIFs), and advisors to offshore funds has reported profit at Rs 79.7 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026, soaring 33.8 percent from Rs 59.5 crore in previous financial year. Its revenue increased 11.1 percent to Rs 135.5 crore from Rs 122 crore during the same period.

JM Financial, and IIFL Capital Services are acting as the merchant bankers for the Gaja Capital IPO.

1.headline: Tempsens Instruments IPO GMP surges to 56% ahead of issue opening on Thursday; check key details
1.heading: Tempsens Instruments IPO GMP surges to 56% ahead of issue opening on Thursday; check key details
1.intro: Tempsens Instruments equity shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE on August 28.
1.body:
Tempsens Instruments IPO grey market premium (GMP) surged to 56 percent ahead of the issue opening on Thursday, according to platforms tracking grey market activity.

Investorgain quoted a GMP of Rs 168 for the shares of Tempsens Instruments, indicating a listing gain of 56 percent. IPO Watch, meanwhile, quoted a GMP of 51.33 percent.

Temperature sensing and heating solutions provider Tempsens Instruments (India) Ltd will launch its initial public offering (IPO) on August 20. The issue size has been pegged at Rs 650 crore.

The price band has been fixed at Rs 285-300 per equity share, while the issue will close on August 24. Bidding by anchor investors will take place on August 19, according to a public announcement on Monday.

The company proposes to utilise the proceeds from the issue towards funding certain capital expenditure for its electrical heating solutions and specialised cable solutions, repayment of debt and general corporate purposes.

Incorporated in 1990, Tempsens is a thermal engineering and specialised cable manufacturer offering customised temperature sensing, electrical heating and specialised cable solutions. The company manufactures a range of contact and non-contact temperature sensors and provides tailored solutions for industrial applications.

The equity shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE on August 28.

2.headline: Maha Transco kicks off search for merchant bankers to steer its landmark power sector IPO
2.heading: Maha Transco kicks off search for merchant bankers to steer its landmark power sector IPO
2.intro: The MSETCL listing will be a significant step in the state government's broader asset monetization drive
2.body:
Maharashtra State Electricity Transmission Company Limited (MSETCL), the state's largest power transmission utility, has formally invited bids from merchant bankers to steer what could become one of India's most closely watched public sector listings in the power sector.

The company issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) on Tuesday seeking to appoint up to six Book Running Lead Managers (BRLMs) to manage its proposed Initial Public Offering, as the Government of Maharashtra moves ahead with plans to monetize its stake in the transmission giant.

A transmission behemoth eyes the market

MSETCL is wholly owned by MSEB Holding Company Limited, the apex state entity overseeing Maharashtra's power sector, and operates as both a licensed transmission utility and the state's designated transmission authority. The company owns and operates over 52,800 circuit kilometres of transmission lines and 760 extra-high-voltage substations, making it one of the largest state transmission utilities in the country.

According to the RFP, the state government is considering monetizing several of its assets, including its holding in MSETCL, and the company is now evaluating an IPO that could combine an offer for sale of government shares with fresh equity issuance. Any final decision remains subject to cabinet approval.

Eligibility bar for merchant bankers

To qualify, bidding merchant bankers must be registered as Category-I entities with the Securities and Exchange Board of India and must have handled at least three domestic equity offerings, including at least one public-sector issue worth Rs 1,000 crore or more, between April 2021 and June 2026, or alternatively have managed a cumulative issue volume of Rs 20,000 crore or more over that period. Bidders must also be free of regulatory action, blacklisting, or debarment.

Also read: SEBI settlement does not bar stock exchange from imposing SOP fine on same LODR violation, says SAT 

The financials behind the listing 

The government-owned public utility has an authorised share capital of Rs 15,000 crore and a paid-up share capital of Rs 8,984 crore.  In FY24, Maha Transco reported an annual profit before tax of Rs 2,738 crore, up 75 percent from Rs 1,564 crore in the previous year. The company’s revenue in FY24 rose to Rs 7210 crore from Rs 5,682 crore in the year before that period. MSETCL derives roughly 86 percent of its revenue from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL), whose weaker credit profile exposes MSETCL to concentrated counterparty risk, though as collection periods have been improving. MSETCL has virtual monopoly over intra-state power transmission in country's most industrialized state.

Evaluation Process

The RFP lays out a competitive selection process combining a technical evaluation (70 percent weight) with financial bids (30 percent weight). Winning bankers will be paid through a fee pool split evenly between a fixed component and a variable component tied to funds mobilized from institutional investors.

The bid schedule is compressed, as per the RFP documents. Pre-bid queries are due by August 24, a pre-bid meeting is scheduled for September 1, and bids must be submitted by 5:00 pm on September 4, 2026. Shortlisted bidders will present their credentials to the company's Empowered Committee for IPO between September 9 and 11.
